A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WavTokenizer work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, allowing methods, equations, figures, tables, and relocated material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction experiments, ARCH classification results, downstream TTS evaluations, and component ablations in Tables 1–9.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds sampling-rate experiments, reconstruction-speed measurements, and objective TTS results in Tables 10–12.

M1.justification: The encoder, single-quantizer codebook procedure, attention-equipped Fourier decoder, discriminators, and training losses remain unchanged. Appendix G trains sampling-rate variants with the existing procedure rather than introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds an explicitly evaluated zero-shot TTS scenario using VALL-E-continue settings and prompt-to-generated speaker matching, beyond v2's general TTS evaluation. Existing corpus, domain, and ARCH task coverage is retained; the sampling-rate experiments reuse existing speech data.

E2.justification: SemantiCodec, previously discussed only as related work, becomes an evaluated comparator in the new reconstruction-speed comparison alongside Encodec and DAC in Table 11. Existing comparison sets remain unchanged, and Table 12 retains DAC as the TTS comparator.

E3.justification: Appendices G–I add targeted protocols: 16/48 kHz training with fixed 320-fold downsampling, reconstruction timing measured by real-time factor, and WER plus WavLM speaker-similarity evaluation under VALL-E-continue settings. Existing training budgets, dataset splits, and subjective evaluation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds a sampling-rate sensitivity analysis examining reconstruction metrics at 16, 24, and 48 kHz. The existing codebook, context-window, decoder, discriminator, attention, and training-data ablations in Section 4.3 and Appendices D–E are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains the same plus/minus reporting, and Appendix C retains its annotation and sampling procedures. The new results introduce no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-estimation practices.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9 retain their numerical results. New Table 10 reports 16/48 kHz UTMOS scores of 3.9606/3.9582; Table 11 reports RTF values of 0.0098 for WavTokenizer, 0.0144 for DAC, 0.0175 for Encodec, and 0.9483 for SemantiCodec. Table 12 adds WavTokenizer/DAC WER of 5.1%/6.9% and speaker similarity of 0.61/0.59. These are supplementary outcomes, not improvements over v2 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1–7 are unchanged, with no added assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations. Definitions of the added empirical evaluation measures do not constitute a theoretical contribution.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of single-quantizer compression to 40 or 75 tokens per second, high perceptual reconstruction quality, semantic richness, and downstream generative usefulness. The new appendix evidence supports these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix G newly interprets relatively stable UTMOS across sampling rates as suggesting stable perceived quality. Appendix H attributes fast reconstruction to inverse Fourier synthesis and low bitrate. The existing limitation concerning weaker ASR-style understanding remains unchanged.

D1.justification: The additions specify a single NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU for timing and WavLM base-plus-sv for speaker embeddings. The front matter now advertises code and checkpoints, whereas v2 advertised available code and promised pretrained models. Existing implementation and optimizer details are retained.

R1.justification: The reference list and substantive related-work discussion are unchanged. SemantiCodec and VALL-E were already cited; their new experimental roles do not introduce new cited works or revise the central novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v3 updates publication headers and author-contribution notes, relocates and expands the acknowledgments, makes limited wording edits, and adds Appendices G–I. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a dedicated dataset column and revised sizing and shading; other tables receive spacing and rule changes. Table 4 moves from page 10 to page 9, and Tables 10–12 are added. Figures 1–2 retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's subjective TTS evidence, Table 12 adds objective intelligibility and speaker-similarity measurements, while Tables 10–11 document sampling-rate behavior and practical speed. These additions modestly strengthen empirical support. Their value is limited by incomplete timing/TTS protocol details and Table 10's inconsistent dataset naming: its caption says Librispeech, whereas Appendix G specifies LibriTTS.
